description: Pedal Forge evaluation set. Expected answers are the author's judgement (provenance: chosen), not ground truth. Questions not listed under an item's expected answers are not scored for it.

items.description: Warm, round bass overdrive that keeps the low end clean underneath.
items.reasoning: Names bass and overdrive. 'Warm, round' points to smooth or tube-like saturation rather than hard clipping. 'Keeps the low end clean underneath' is the clean-blend case. Overdrive rather than distortion suggests light to moderate drive.

items.description: Guitar sound that is clean when I play softly and just starts to break up when I dig in.
items.reasoning: Describes the edge of break-up level exactly. Touch-sensitive break-up is a soft-knee behaviour, so soft or asymmetric tanh.

items.description: Completely clean, pristine guitar with no distortion at all.
items.reasoning: Explicitly no distortion and nothing about tone, so no filter.

items.description: Just tighten up the lows on my bass a little, it is too boomy in this room.
items.reasoning: Asks only to reduce boom, which is a high-pass. No drive asked for. 'Tighten' here is about the filter, not the clipping knee.

items.description: Dark, mellow clean guitar tone with the treble rolled off for slow ballads.
items.reasoning: Treble rolled off is a low-pass; dark and mellow put brightness at the dark end.

items.description: Tight, aggressive high-gain guitar distortion for fast palm-muted riffs.
items.reasoning: High gain with tightness and aggression suggests a firm knee clipper at a heavy setting.

items.description: Huge saturated fuzz guitar, a wall of sound that is almost square.
items.reasoning: Saturated and near-square is the top level. The shaper is left open: several variants reach a square wave when driven this hard.

items.description: Growling bass drive with pushed mids so it cuts through a loud band.
items.reasoning: Pushed mids to cut through is a mid boost via the peaking EQ. Growl is more than a hint of drive.

items.description: Scooped, hollow guitar distortion with the mids cut right back.
items.reasoning: Mid cut is the peaking EQ with negative gain.

items.description: Dreamy shimmering reverb on clean guitar.
items.reasoning: Reverb is not in the block vocabulary, so the plugin should say so rather than build a partial chain.

items.description: Add an octave below my bass notes for a synth-like sub.
items.reasoning: Pitch shifting is not in the vocabulary.

items.description: Short slapback echo on a twangy clean guitar.
items.reasoning: Echo is a delay, which is not in the vocabulary.

items.description: Lush chorus on a clean guitar for arpeggios.
items.reasoning: Chorus is modulation, not in the vocabulary.

items.description: Clean, natural bass, just as it is, maybe a touch brighter.
items.reasoning: No drive. 'A touch brighter' is just above neutral. The filter type is left open because a gentle lift could be a high shelf, which the vocabulary lacks, or no filter.

items.description: Fuzzy, buzzy bass with the clean low end blended back in so it does not lose weight.
items.reasoning: Blending the clean low end back in is the keep-lows path. Fuzz puts drive high.

items.description: Broken, sputtering lo-fi guitar that sounds like a dying speaker.
items.reasoning: Uneven, broken clipping matches the soft-above, hard-below variant. A dying speaker is at least moderate drive.

items.description: Thin telephone-style guitar for an intro, very little bass and lots of upper mids.
items.reasoning: A telephone sound removes lows and emphasises upper mids. Either a high-pass or a mid peak is a reasonable single filter. Drive is unclear and not scored.

items.description: Thick, warm tube-like crunch with lots of even harmonics.
items.reasoning: Even harmonics come from asymmetric clipping. Crunch is the moderate level.

items.description: Very subtle grit on bass, you should barely notice it until you play hard.
items.reasoning: Barely noticeable until played hard is the edge of break-up.

items.description: Bright, crisp, sparkly clean guitar for funk rhythm.
items.reasoning: Bright and sparkly put brightness at the top, without drive. Filter type left open.

items.description: Very dark, woolly dub bass with almost no treble.
items.reasoning: Almost no treble is a strong low-pass and the darkest level.

items.description: Make it sound angrier.
items.reasoning: Short and vague. Angrier most plausibly means more distortion. The instrument is not named, so it is not scored; a good model should be unsure about it.

items.description: Make it sound better.
items.reasoning: Deliberately vague: nothing is scored except that it needs nothing outside the vocabulary. A calibrated model should give low confidence on most questions, and the plugin should fall back to defaults or ask.

items.description: Modern metal bass: tight, hard clipping on the top end, with the lows kept clean and tight.
items.reasoning: Hard clipping and tightness suggest the knee clipper; lows kept clean is the blend path; metal is heavy.

items.description: Smooth, creamy, singing lead guitar with long sustain.
items.reasoning: Creamy sustain needs fair drive with a soft knee. The filter is left open.

items.description: Funky wah on clean guitar.
items.reasoning: A wah is a swept filter controlled by a pedal or envelope. The vocabulary has only static filters, so it should count as out of vocabulary.

items.description: Honky, nasal midrange bass tone for a punk band, slightly overdriven.
items.reasoning: Honky and nasal is a mid boost. Slightly overdriven is low to moderate drive.

items.description: My distortion is too fizzy, smooth out the top end.
items.reasoning: Too fizzy on a distorted sound asks for a low-pass after the shaper. The player already has distortion, so a waveshaper stays.

items.description: Leave my bass flat and clean, I only want a safety limiter.
items.reasoning: Explicitly nothing; the limiter is always present anyway.

items.description: Overdriven guitar with a pulsing tremolo.
items.reasoning: Tremolo is modulation and is not in the vocabulary, even though the drive part is.

items.description: Add a gentle warmth to clean guitar, like a good amp just starting to work.
items.reasoning: Gentle warmth is light saturation from a soft shaper. Whether that counts as clean or the edge of break-up is unclear, so both are accepted.

items.description: Square-wave, synth-like bass fuzz with the low end kept intact.
items.reasoning: Square wave is maximum saturation. Low end intact is the blend path.

items.description: Rhythm guitar that cuts through a busy mix, moderate crunch.
items.reasoning: Cutting through a mix is a mid push. Moderate crunch is level 2.

items.description: Remove the mud from my overdriven bass without losing the punch.
items.reasoning: Mud sits in the low mids. A gentle high-pass or a low-mid cut both answer it. Losing punch argues against an aggressive high-pass, but the filter type is the scored part.

items.description: Swirling rotary speaker sound on an organ-like guitar part.
items.reasoning: A rotary speaker is modulation, not in the vocabulary.

items.description: Gritty, ragged, uneven bass distortion that sounds broken in a good way.
items.reasoning: Ragged, uneven clipping matches the soft-above, hard-below variant.

items.description: Glassy, very bright clean guitar, almost piercing.
items.reasoning: Very bright and piercing is the top level.

items.description: Warm fingerstyle bass for soul, darker than usual, no dirt.
items.reasoning: Darker than usual is one step dark; no dirt means no drive.

items.description: Heavy, dark, doom-style guitar distortion, thick and slow.
items.reasoning: Heavy and dark on both axes. Thick might suggest asymmetric clipping, but the shaper is left open.

items.description: Loop my bass line and layer distorted parts on top.
items.reasoning: Looping is outside the vocabulary.
